solution: Let \(E\) = persons who speak English, \(F\) = persons who speak French. Given \(n(E)=72\), \(n(F)=43\), and since each of the 100 persons speaks at least one language, \(n(E \cup F)=100\). Using \(n(E \cup F)=n(E)+n(F)-n(E \cap F)\): \(100=72+43-n(E \cap F)\), so \(n(E \cap F)=115-100=15\). Only English \(=n(E)-n(E \cap F)=72-15=57\). Only French \(=n(F)-n(E \cap F)=43-15=28\). Only English \(=57\), only French \(=28\), both English and French \(=15\).

Let \(A\) = trees planted by Parth, \(B\) = trees planted by Pradnya. Given \(n(A)=70\), \(n(B)=90\), \(n(A \cap B)=25\). Trees planted by Parth or Pradnya \(=n(A \cup B)=n(A)+n(B)-n(A \cap B)=70+90-25=135\). \(n(A \cup B)=135\).
Total students \(=28\). Students having a dog or cat \(=\) (only dog) \(+\) (only cat) \(+\) (both) \(=8+6+10=24\). Students who do not have a dog or cat \(=28-24=4\). \(4\) students.

solution: \(P=\{a, b, c, e, f\}\), \(Q=\{l, m, n, e, b\}\). The common elements \(b, e\) go in the overlap; \(a, c, f\) in the P-only region and \(l, m, n\) in the Q-only region. \(P \cup Q=\{a, b, c, e, f, l, m, n\}\).

solution: Prime numbers between 80 and 100 give \(X=\{83, 89, 97\}\). Odd numbers between 90 and 100 give \(Y=\{91, 93, 95, 97, 99\}\). The common element \(97\) goes in the overlap; \(83, 89\) in the X-only region and \(91, 93, 95, 99\) in the Y-only region. \(X \cup Y=\{83, 89, 91, 93, 95, 97, 99\}\).
diagramNote: Two overlapping ovals X and Y: X-only = 83, 89; overlap (X∩Y) = 97; Y-only = 91, 93, 95, 99. The whole shaded region is X∪Y.

solution: The empty set has no elements, so uniting it with \(M\) adds nothing and intersecting it with \(M\) shares nothing. \(M \cup \varnothing=M\) and \(M \cap \varnothing=\varnothing\).

The universal set is every element inside the rectangle: \(U=\{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13\}\). Set \(A\) is the A-only region together with the overlap: \(A=\{1, 2, 3, 5, 7\}\). Set \(B\) is the B-only region together with the overlap: \(B=\{1, 5, 8, 9, 10\}\). \(A \cup B=\{1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10\}\) and \(A \cap B=\{1, 5\}\).
diagramNote: Rectangle U with two overlapping ovals A and B: A-only = 2, 3, 7; overlap (A∩B) = 1, 5; B-only = 8, 9, 10; outside both ovals but inside U = 4, 11, 13.
